summary.judge:
===RULE NOTES===
1. **Adherence:** perfect — 40/40 outputs are single bare instruction lines, fourth consecutive clean eval. **Performance:** nothing to measure when it never misfires. Per the operator correction, the "Thinking Process:" leaks it was written against were never this applier's failure — the rule's anti-leak clause is insurance against a hazard this pipeline doesn't have. **What to do:** keep it anyway, unchanged. Its real load-bearing part for this applier is the copy-the-input fallback (which rules 4 and 2 both lean on), it costs nothing, and rewording a rule that has never failed spends evidence-continuity for no gain. Drop the "Thinking Process:" example only if the book ever needs trimming for length.

2. **Adherence: perfect for the first time in four books.** All 26 qualifying bases passed through character-exact at delta +0.000 — including every historical slip victim present in the sample: 'put fork from basket to tray' (rewritten in three prior books at -0.97/-0.38/-0.14/-0.27), 'put the silver lid on the silver pot' (detail-dropped at -0.22 under the regressed book), 'Shut the drawer.', 'flatten the blue cloth from top down'. The restored hard wall ("output it exactly as given: do not…") achieved what the softened "you may make exactly one kind of change" version could not. **Performance:** the wall's known price was paid in plain sight: 'Lift the pot up out of the washbasin.' passed through at 0.000 where the withdrawn exception once earned +3.566 — that single base accounts for -0.089 of the book's eval delta vs the regressed book. That trade was the deliberate bet: forgo a rare +3.57 to eliminate the at-scale slop tax (≈-2.2 summed) the exception licensed. **The eval sample cannot settle this bet** — the slop only appeared across the wider outcome pool, so this book sitting -0.028 below the regressed book on the eval sample (+0.516 vs +0.544) is expected and uninformative; validation is the arbiter. **What to do:** hold the wording exactly. If validation confirms this book beats the regressed one, the wall-plus-no-exception design is settled. The washbasin family's earn-back path stands as written last round: pure same-draw washbasin/sink and fabric/cloth pairs (still unmeasured — the probes were requested and did not run) plus demonstrated zero unlicensed edits; until then the +3.57 stays forgone on purpose.

3. **Adherence:** clean on all 14 rewrites — short, verb-first, plain, several lowercase (case measured neutral previously; the lowercase carton rewrite actually drew +1.115 where its capitalized twin drew +0.539, cross-draw noise favoring nobody). **Performance:** the rewrite set is the strongest yet where it obeyed: sample mean +0.860, every changed delta positive, minimum +0.028. **What to do:** keep word for word, fifth book running.

4. **Adherence:** full. Both spatula circumlocutions decoded (+5.670/+5.268), "hemispherical dish"→'lift the bowl' (+2.389 — better than every prior version of this rewrite, and with nothing invented), the ambiguous "handled cooking vessel" decoded to pot per the ordinary-word clause (+1.710; the pan reading is worth ~1.0 more but is unknowable from the base), and "red object" kept verbatim again. No guessed objects anywhere in-sample; the garbled-glass base didn't appear this round, so the copy-if-unintelligible fallback remains untested at eval level (its outcome-file record: the loss shrank from -2.57/-2.11 to -0.79 under this wording). **Performance:** engine of the book, as always. **What to do:** keep word for word.

5. **Adherence: full, at last — and the fix that got it there is worth generalizing.** The rule's inline example was executed verbatim: 'the orange, cone-shaped vegetable' → 'the orange carrot' (+1.018, matching the probe's 7.738 prediction for the fragment-free form after two books of "cone-shaped" surviving). The box rewrite shed 'projecting/atop/miniature' → 'fold the four flaps on the small box' (+3.213, the best of that rewrite's four measured versions). No invented locations ('lift the bowl', not 'from the counter'), both "silver"s protected via pass-through, the conditional preamble dropped (+3.633), "or the pan" untouched. Zero detail drops in the entire sample — the failure mode that sank the regressed book is gone in-sample. **Performance:** every clause now has a measured win behind it. **What to do:** keep word for word. The lesson to carry forward (for the rulebook author, not this rule): the clause that finally worked is the one whose example names the exact recurring failure — "never drop one it does state" was ignored for two books while "'the orange, cone-shaped vegetable' → 'the orange carrot'" was executed on first contact. Rules earn adherence through concrete examples, not emphasis.

6. **Adherence:** good with one soft spot. Small words held ("up" survived via the washbasin no-op; "from A to B" kept everywhere), two linked commands used in all four transfer rewrites. The soft spot: the red-object rewrite chose 'pick up the red object **from** the pot and put it on the left burner' (5.423, +2.781) where the regressed book's 'take the red object **out of** the pot…' hit 7.806 (+5.163) — a ~2.4-logit gap on the same base, cross-draw. Rule 6 lists take and pick up as equals and says nothing about "out of" vs "from" for container removal, so this was compliant behavior with a costly free choice. **Performance:** when its preferences bound, they paid (+5.670/+3.633 two-command wins); where it was silent, the applier left ~2.4 logits on one base. **What to do:** do not reword yet — the out-of/from contrast rests on one cross-draw pair, and "from" is corpus-normal in other frames ('put fork from basket to tray' is a canonical task string), so a blanket preference could backfire. Run the paired probe below first; if it confirms ≥1 logit, next book should append to rule 6: "when the object comes out of or off a container, write 'take X out of A and put it on B', not 'pick up X from A'."

7. **Adherence: perfect — and the mandate upgrade paid exactly as the probe predicted.** The applier produced the caption form verbatim: 'end effector transition from the first piece to the second piece', measuring 8.096 in situ (probe: 8.163) for **+6.897, the largest delta ever recorded in these evals** — vs +6.038 for the term-substitution the old wording allowed and -1.16/-0.73 for the books before the rule existed. The never-translate guard had nothing to violate in-sample. **What to do:** keep word for word; this rule is finished. The only residual question — whether the rule generalizes to the "end effector reaching X" caption family — has never been exercised by any base in the samples; it would only matter if such bases exist in the validation pool, and a probe below covers the cheap check.

**Book-level:** +0.516 on the eval sample (best book +0.408, regressed book +0.544). The -0.028 vs the regressed book decomposes almost exactly into the two deliberate/known items: the forgone washbasin exception (-0.089) and the red-object verb choice (-0.060), partially offset by the caption mandate (+0.021), the fragment fix (+0.004 net of draw), the cleaner lift-bowl and carton rewrites (+0.030). Everything the repair was designed to eliminate — detail drops, article insertion, synonym slop, pass-through violations — is absent from this sample entirely, and that benefit lives at validation scale, not eval scale. No rules pulled against each other anywhere in the sample: 2 and 5 now jointly protect details, 4 and 5 split the carrot rewrite cleanly, and 7 overrode 4's keep-"robot hand" clause correctly. This is the first eval where every rule was simultaneously obeyed.

===SUGGESTIONS===
Measure 'take the red object out of the pot and put it on the left burner' and 'pick up the red object from the pot and put it on the left burner' as a same-draw pair — prices the out-of/from choice rule 6 currently leaves free (cross-draw gap ~2.4 logits); confirms or kills the proposed rule-6 clause.
Measure 'Lift the pot up out of the washbasin.' vs 'Lift the pot up out of the sink.' as a pure same-draw pair — the withdrawn rule-2 exception's honest price, requested twice and never run; needed for any future earn-back decision.
Measure 'Take the piece of fabric on the left and put it on the right.' vs 'Take the piece of cloth on the left and put it on the right.' — the fabric half of the same earn-back question (one outcome draw showed -0.242 for the swap; a paired number would settle it).
Measure 'pick up the spatula and put it on top of the plate in the sink' — completes the preposition grid: the applier's produced variants scored 6.933 ('on the top of…at the sink') and 7.331 ('on the plate in the sink') while the short-form probe hit 7.975 ('on top of…in the sink'); tells us whether ~0.6 logit rides on the preposition scaffold inside the two-command frame.
Measure 'end effector reaching the corn' on the end-effector-reaching-corn task family if it is probeable — cheap check that rule 7's caption style generalizes beyond the transition task before anyone widens the rule.
Measure 'put the silver lid on the silver pot' vs 'put the lid on the pot' as a same-draw pair — the detail-drop cost rule 5 guards against has only one outcome-draw number (-0.217); a controlled pair makes the wall's value citable.
